label: input w in the middle of the original phase (steps 3-6)
explanation: Fires only during the original-input phase, never at t<2, the delimiter or copy phase. Its main trigger is the letter w as input (72% of activation mass, 18x lift), mostly at steps 3-6 with a peak at t=4. The strongest activations are almost all w inputs (88% coverage of the top quartile), often when a second w follows an earlier one. A weaker, diffuse tail fires on t and y (about 8% of mass each) and occasionally on e, b, u and other tokens. Precision is limited because many mid-sequence w inputs stay inactive. Whether a w fires depends strongly on the first original token: sequences starting with r, 1, h, f, p, z, x or 2 give about 95% precision but cover only about 35% of mass. I did not find a clean rule for this sequence-level dependence. It does not fire on w at steps 0-1 or on any delimiter or copy-phase step.
